title: Semiconductors, BJTs and FETs
blurb: Explain doping and the PN junction, bipolar beta, and how FETs differ, and read the six FET symbols.

E6A01.why: GaAs electrons move fast, so it suits **microwave** circuits.
E6A01.trap: Rectifiers and low-frequency work are silicon's territory.

E6A02.why: **Donor** impurities add free electrons, making N-type (negative carriers).
E6A02.trap: P-type has an excess of holes, not electrons.

E6A03.why: Reverse voltage pulls holes and electrons away from the junction, **widening the depletion region** until it blocks current.
E6A03.trap: Both materials conduct on their own; the empty junction zone is what blocks.

E6A04.why: An impurity that creates holes accepts electrons: an **acceptor**. Donors give electrons.

E6A05.why: A FET gate is insulated or reverse-biased, so it draws almost no current: **high input impedance**.
E6A05.trap: A BJT base draws current, so its input impedance is lower.

E6A06.why: Beta is the **change in collector current per change in base current**: the transistor's current gain.
E6A06.trap: Frequency where gain falls to 0.707 is a cutoff frequency, not beta.

E6A07.why: A forward-biased silicon junction drops about **0.6 to 0.7 volts**. It is a voltage, not an ohmic resistance.
E6A07.trap: 6 to 7 V is ten times too high. A junction is judged by its voltage drop, not by ohms.

E6A08.why: Grounded-base gain is **alpha**, so the frequency where it falls to 0.7 is the **alpha cutoff** frequency.
E6A08.trap: Beta cutoff refers to common-emitter gain.

E6A09.why: Depletion mode: the channel is already open, so **current flows with zero gate voltage**.
E6A09.trap: No current at zero gate volts describes enhancement mode.

E6A10.why: Two gate leads (G1, G2) mean dual-gate; an arrow pointing at the channel bar means N-channel.
E6A10.trap: Dual-gate symbols with the arrow pointing away are P-channel.

E6A11.why: A JFET has a plain channel bar with the gate arrow on it. Arrow pointing **away** from the bar means P-channel.
E6A11.trap: Arrow pointing at the bar is N-channel; a gate plate set apart is a MOSFET.

E6A12.why: The gate oxide is extremely thin. A Zener clamps voltage spikes to **protect the gate from static damage**.
E6A12.trap: It is not a reference or heat limiter; it only clamps damaging spikes.
